methods.name: Spatial GMM (Kelejian-Prucha): spatial 2SLS, GM + FGLS error model, GS2SLS SARAR; classical, White and spatial-HAC SEs; SE of rho
methods.reference: Kelejian & Prucha (1998, 1999, 2007, 2010) written out in base R (sphet/spdep not installed); kernels, HAC, heteroskedastic GM moments and the Psi of the rho variance follow sphet 2.1-1 (kernelsfun.R, twostagels.R, gm_functions.R)
quantities: SE spatial HAC, fixed bandwidth (triangular at d = 0.15 and 0.30; Epanechnikov, rectangular, bisquare, Parzen, Tukey-Hanning and quadratic spectral at d = 0.15)
methods.tolerance: validation/README.md, n = 150: closed-form 2SLS coefficients 1e-8 and SEs 1e-6 relative; GM rho and everything after it Tol::iterative(1e-8) (exact R minimiser; Rust safeguarded Newton to a 1e-10 relative step); SE of rho 1e-6

deviations.note: The variable bandwidth takes W's neighbour sets as the distance object (each unit's farthest W-neighbour); sphet takes a separate sphet::distance object. The case writes out the p2a definition.
alpha_r = 0, its value under exogenous X (Kelejian-Prucha 2010, Theorem 2); sphet's Psi plugs in the sample alpha_r, which is O_p(n^-1/2), so the two differ by O(1/n) relative.
rho is the step-1 identity-weighted GM estimate, with its valid sandwich SE; sphet's gstslshet adds the efficient step with Psi^-1 weights.
The Kelejian-Prucha (1999) three moments; sphet's spreg(het = FALSE) uses the Drukker et al. two-moment version.
[-0.99, 0.99]; sphet's nlminb bounds are (-0.9, 0.9), which cut off valid estimates in [0.9, 0.99).
